newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast prods prices steady to higher late.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast prods prices steady to higher late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices were steady to slightly higher late Friday, with a modest rise in NYMEX crude futures countered by razor-thin pre-holiday trade.
Los Angeles CARB gasoline stayed unchanged at 69.50 and 70.50 cents a gallon. Bay area grade stayed 3.50 cents cheaper.
Meanwhile, conventional unleaded in L.A. made a 0.50 gain in late trade to 67/68 cents a gallon.
Market activity was slow early as players left early for the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
NYMEX will be closed Monday for the holiday.
Ongoing concerns about low heating oil stocks lent strength to distillate prices early, with the American Petroleum Institute showing a 463,000 barrel fall last week.
But Los Angeles low sulphur diesel was flat late at 69/70 cents and the CARB grade added at half cent to reach 72.50/73.50 cents a gallon.
Bay distillates were one cent higher than L.A..
